title: Power-up visibility HUD — icon grid + pickup tooltip + opponent active-state badges (no more guessing what you have)
intent: User feedback 2026-05-27: 'непонятно какими повер-апами владеет игрок, приходится гадать'. The current HUD packs power-up state as text flags inside the per-bomber row ('bombs 1/3 fire 2 K R S P') — readable, but it's TEXT in a 14px monospace corner cell, requiring the player to read rather than scan. With Kick, Remote, Shield, Pierce shipped (and Throw Glove + Bomb Pass + Pierce-bomb + more upcoming), the flag list will grow past readable density. This story replaces text flags with an ICON GRID + a momentary PICKUP TOOLTIP + opponent ACTIVE-STATE BADGES — giving the player at-a-glance recognition of their own power-up state without losing the tactical guessing layer for opponents.
rationale: Source: user feedback 2026-05-27 + `docs/game-design/visual-style.md §1` (Gameplay readability is the #1 pillar: 'every game-important element must be readable in under 200 ms of gaze') + §8.3 (icon set already specified as mono cream silhouettes). Text flags violate the 200ms-gaze rule — three or four letter flags need 400-600ms to parse. As the power-up catalogue grows past the current 7 kinds (bomb-up, fire-up, speed-up, kick, remote, shield, pierce + future Throw, Bomb Pass), the text approach breaks down. Sized `should` because the current text HUD is functional (just barely), but every playtest session with the user has now surfaced this as friction.
acceptanceHints: Three coordinated layers — all needed; partial implementation leaves the gap user noticed.
LAYER 1 — Self HUD icon grid (replaces the current text-flag row for the LOCAL player):
Bottom-left HUD region. The 'Round N | W:A L:B D:C' line stays at the top of the panel (round metadata). Below it, a 2-row grid of power-up slots:

Row 1 (numeric power-ups, always visible): bomb / fire / speed icons. Each icon + a 'CURRENT/MAX' badge — e.g. '🎒 3/6' (bombs), '🔥 4/8' (range), '👟 3/5' (speed). The number under the icon is the bomber's current level in that stat.

Row 2 (binary power-ups, lock-state visible): kick / remote / shield / pierce / throw-glove / bomb-pass icons. Each is FULL-COLOUR + glow ring when active; DESATURATED + 30% opacity when not yet picked up.
All icons are mono cream silhouettes per visual-style.md §8.3 — 24×24 px each, 4 px gap. Total panel size ~ 200×80 px (fits below the current round/tally row).
Active state visual: the bomber's primary palette colour tints the icon's accent edge. Reinforces 'this is YOUR HUD'.
Per-bomber primary palette colour pulled from recipe.palette.head (already established).
LAYER 2 — Pickup tooltip (transient, learns the player the icon→pickup mapping):
On any pickup-collect: a centre-screen tooltip banner appears for 1.5s with the icon (4x size — 96×96 px) + a label ('KICK!' / 'FIRE UP +1' / 'SHIELD' / etc.) + a fade-in (0.15s) + fade-out (0.30s).
Banner position: just above the HUD bottom-left, NOT centre-screen (centre is reserved for round-resolve banner per gameplay-systems.md §6 and visual-style.md §8.2).
Bomber's primary palette tint on the banner border.

Cap: ONE active tooltip at a time. If a player collects pickup B while pickup A's tooltip is showing → fast-fade-out A (0.10s) then show B. Prevents tooltip queueing — players who chain pickups see the latest.
Audio coupling: existing 'pickup' clip + vocal-synth 'pickup' utterance still fires (no new audio).
LAYER 3 — Opponent active-state badges (over remote bomber heads in multiplayer + solo's other bombers):
Small icon strip floating above each non-local bomber's head — world-space, billboarded toward camera.
Shows ONLY DISCRETE ACTIVE STATES: Shield (when active), Pierce, Throw Glove (when carrying a bomb), Remote (when has armed bomb).

Does NOT show: numeric power-up counts (bombs/fire/speed levels) — preserves the tactical guessing layer per `gameplay-systems.md §14 Open questions #2` ('removes a did they place another? guessing layer').
Does NOT show: Kick (passive — kick doesn't change behavior visibly until used; revealing it pre-use is over-information).

Layout: 3-icon horizontal strip max (Shield, Pierce, Remote, Throw — picks any active ones, deterministic order). 16×16 px each. White-on-dark cream-stroke palette (NOT bomber's hue — opponents read as opponents, not as your own colour).
Hidden when all opponent active-states are false → no badge strip, no clutter.
ICON ART:

Generated procedurally from primitives via a small SVG generator OR pulled from CC0 sources (Kenney's UI pack is recommended starting point — `kenney_ui-pack` has bomb, fire, boot, target icons compatible).
Per visual-style.md §8.3 strict: no emoji, monochrome cream silhouettes, no rounded corners (industrial = hard edges).
Icon list needed: bomb, fire, boot/speed, kick-boot (different from speed-boot — kick has impact lines), remote-trigger, shield, pierce-arrow, throw-glove, bomb-pass-wavy (future).
If procedural-svg-generator is too much scope for one sprint, ship CC0 sources directly into the kaboom-crew project's assets dir.
MULTIPLAYER:
Server's snapshot already carries BomberStats for every Presence entity (S117-S125 Sprint B). Client reads opponent BomberStats and renders the badges from there.
Local player HUD: from local BomberStats (unchanged path).
Tooltip: fires locally only (no network event needed — server's snapshot of an updated BomberStats triggers the local tooltip on the corresponding pickup-collect event).
DEAD BOMBER BEHAVIOUR:
Local bomber dies → HUD freezes at the at-death state (player can see what they had). Reset to defaults on round-restart.
Remote bomber dies → badges fade out alongside the ragdoll (same 0.6s).
EDGE CASES:
Bomber picks up same powerup twice (e.g. kick when already canKick=true): NO tooltip (it's a no-op gameplay-wise). Audio 'pickup' still fires for the sound feedback.
Multiple pickups in a single fixedUpdate (rare but legal): show LATEST pickup's tooltip; earlier ones get the 'fast-fade' replacement treatment.

Throw-Glove active state badge: shows whenever bomber.canThrow=true (i.e. they have the power-up). The 'currently carrying a bomb' sub-state (per GDP-2026-05-26-004 acceptance) is a DIFFERENT badge — a small '!' or bomb-icon overlay on the throw-glove badge when carrying. Document this nesting clearly so the dev doesn't ship just a static throw-glove badge.
ACCESSIBILITY:
All numeric badges include alt-text (aria-label on the HUD canvas elements) — readable by screen reader for accessibility-mode playtest.
Icons have a 1-pixel cream outline against the dark HUD panel — readable for low-vision users.
No flashing/pulsing — icons are static once their state stabilises. The pickup tooltip's fade is gentle (0.15s linear). No epilepsy concern.
UNIT TESTS:
Icon grid renders all 9 slots given a BomberStats with various values. Numeric slots show current/max. Boolean slots show active/inactive state visually distinct.
Tooltip on collect: pickup → tooltip appears within 50ms → fades after 1.5s. Snapshot test on the tooltip's DOM state at key timestamps.
Tooltip overlap: collect A → 200ms later collect B → tooltip B replaces tooltip A within 100ms.
Opponent badges: BomberStats with shield=true + pierce=false → only Shield badge renders. With all 4 binary active → 3 badges (cap to top 3 by priority).
Opponent badges hide when ALL discrete active states are false.
PLAYTEST QA BAR (the user's actual ask):
Mid-game, the user can name every power-up they currently have in ≤ 2 seconds of looking at the HUD. No reading text required.
When the user picks up a new power-up, they correctly identify what it does within 1.5s (during the tooltip).
OUT OF SCOPE:
Opponent numeric power-up counts (bombs A/B, fire C) — stays hidden per gameplay-systems.md §14 deferred-decision recommendation.
Power-up history strip (what's been collected this round). Could be a follow-up if playtest wants it; not in v1.
Customisable HUD layout (player drags icon grid around). Out — fixed bottom-left.
Minimap powerup indicators (icons floating on minimap cells). Out — minimap is for spatial-awareness, not stat-awareness.
Sound on pickup-tooltip-shown (the existing 'pickup' clip + vocal-synth fires already; no new audio).
Tooltip extension to bot pickups in solo mode. Bots collect silently — preserves the 'where did that go' tension.
